content: 1. Clarithromycin and Fentanyl (Intranasal, Transdermal, Transmucosal): Clarithromycin increases the levels and effects of fentanyl by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4, which is responsible for fentanyl metabolism. This interaction can lead to enhanced sedation and respiratory depression. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is necessary, monitor the patient closely for signs of respiratory depression and sedation at frequent intervals. Adjust the fentanyl dose as needed until stable drug effects are achieved. 2. Omeprazole and Ferric Carboxymaltose, Ferric Gluconate, Ferric Maltol, Ferrous Fumarate, Ferrous Gluconate, Ferrous Sulfate: Omeprazole decreases the levels and effects of these iron supplements by increasing gastric pH, which reduces their absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely when coadministering. Adjust therapy as needed. 3. Clarithromycin and Fesoterodine: Clarithromycin increases the levels and effects of fesoterodine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 4. Fexinidazole and Omeprazole: Fexinidazole increases the levels and effects of omeprazole by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Monitor closely for potential adverse effects. 5. Clarithromycin and Fexinidazole: Both drugs increase the QTc interval, which can lead to serious cardiac arrhythmias. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Additionally, clarithromycin decreases the levels and effects of fexinidazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 6. Clarithromycin and Finasteride: Clarithromycin increases the levels and effects of finasteride by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Clarithromycin and Finererone: Clarithromycin increases the levels and effects of finererone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Omeprazole also increases finererone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Modify therapy and monitor serum potassium during initiation and dosage adjustments of finererone or weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. 8. Clarithromycin and Fingolimod: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 9. Clarithromycin and Flecainide: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 10. Clarithromycin and Flibanserin: Clarithromycin increases the levels and effects of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Coadministration of flibanserin with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated due to the risk of hypotension, syncope, and CNS depression. 11. Fluconazole and Omeprazole: Fluconazole increases the levels and effects of omeprazole by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 12. Clarithromycin and Fluconazole: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 13. Clarithromycin and Fludrocortisone: Clarithromycin increases the levels and effects of fludrocortisone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Clarithromycin and Fluoxetine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Monitor closely. 15. Clarithromycin and Flurazepam: Clarithromycin increases the levels and effects of flurazepam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Omeprazole also increases flurazepam levels by decreasing its metabolism. Monitor closely. 16. Clarithromycin and Fluticasone (Furoate, Inhaled, Intranasal): Clarithromycin increases the levels and effects of fluticasone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic corticosteroid exposure, leading to adverse effects such as Cushing syndrome. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Monitor for signs of high corticosteroid concentrations. 17. Clarithromycin and Fluvastatin: Clarithromycin increases the toxicity of fluvastatin, potentially leading to myopathy. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 18. Clarithromycin and Fluvoxamine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 19. Clarithromycin and Fondaparinux: Clarithromycin increases the effects of fondaparinux by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 20. Clarithromycin and Formoterol: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 21. Omeprazole and Fosamprenavir: Omeprazole decreases the levels and effects of fosamprenavir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 22. Clarithromycin and Fosaprepitant: Clarithromycin increases the levels and effects of fosaprepitant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 23. Clarithromycin and Foscarnet: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 24. Clarithromycin and Fostamatinib: Clarithromycin increases the levels and effects of fostamatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase exposure to R406 (the major active metabolite of fostamatinib). Monitor for toxicities and adjust the fostamatinib dose as needed. 25. Clarithromycin and Fostemsavir: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 26. Clarithromycin and Futibatinib: Clarithromycin increases the levels and effects of futibatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 27. Clarithromycin and Gadobenate: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. This combination is contraindicated. 28. Clarithromycin and Ganaxolone: Changes in ganaxolone exposure when coadministered with CYP3A4 inhibitors are not expected to be clinically significant. Monitor closely. 29. Omeprazole and Gefitinib: Omeprazole decreases gefitinib levels by increasing gastric pH. Avoid coadministration if possible. Clarithromycin increases gefitinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 30. Clarithromycin and Gemifloxacin: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 31. Clarithromycin and Gentamicin: Clarithromycin increases the levels and effects of gentamicin by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Clarithromycin and Gepirone: Clarithromycin increases the levels and effects of gepirone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 33. Clarithromycin and Gilteritinib: Clarithromycin increases the levels and effects of gilteritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Monitor ECG if coadministration is necessary. 34. Clarithromycin and Givinostat: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Obtain ECGs during initiation and concomitant use. 35. Clarithromycin and Glasdegib: Clarithromycin increases the levels and effects of glasdegib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 36. Clarithromycin and Glecaprevir/Pibrentasvir: Clarithromycin increases the levels and effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Clarithromycin and Glimepiride, Glipizide, Glyburide: Clarithromycin increases the levels of these drugs by plasma protein binding competition, increasing the risk of hypoglycemia. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Clarithromycin and Goserelin: Goserelin increases the toxicity of clarithromycin by prolonging the QTc interval, increasing the risk of torsades de pointes. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Clarithromycin and Granisetron: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 40. Grapefruit and Clarithromycin: Grapefruit increases clarithromycin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 41. Griseofulvin and Clarithromycin: Griseofulvin decreases clarithromycin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 42. Clarithromycin and Guanfacine: Clarithromycin increases guanfacine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors significantly increase guanfacine plasma concentrations. For extended-release guanfacine, reduce the dose to half the recommended amount. Specific recommendations for immediate-release guanfacine are not available. 43. Clarithromycin and Haloperidol: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 44. Clarithromycin and Heparin: Clarithromycin increases the effects of heparin by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 45. Histrelin and Clarithromycin: Histrelin increases the toxicity of clarithromycin by prolonging the QTc interval, increasing the risk of torsades de pointes. Use caution and monitor closely.
